newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. food summit blunders again.
newsitem.headline: U.N. food summit blunders again.

text.p: The World Food Summit in Rome may go down in history as a landmark in the fight against hunger but it will also be remembered for diplomatic blunders.

In the latest example at the five-day meeting, organisers listed "His Excellency Sheikh Hasina, Prime Minister of Bangladesh" in the official programme as one of the speakers at the summit on Saturday. Hasina is a woman.
Earlier this week, the Philippines' representative suffered a similar fate and was introduced to delegates by the English interpreter as "His Excellency Leticia Ramos-Shahani".
Ramos-Shahani, who is mounting a campaign to succeed Boutros Boutros-Ghali as U.N. Secretary General, is also a woman.

A speech by Israeli Agriculture and Environment Minister Rafael Eitan in Hebrew ground to a halt when the interpreter lost his way. The interpreter admitted he could not read the Hebrew text and Eitan had to start his speech again.

But the most serious blunder in the delicate world of diplomatic protocol came on Friday, when the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) apologised to Chinese Premier Li Peng after identifying him as leader of arch-rival Taiwan in the official programme.
The programme for Friday's session referred to Li as "Premier of the State Council of the Republic of China".
That is the official name of Taiwan, which Beijing does not recognise as an independent country. Communist China's official name is "The People's Republic of China".
